profile.objective: Assess the evidence and capital milestones needed before a financing process.
profile.model_rationale: Cedar is testing a manufactured prototype. Its only inspected run lasted one supervised shift.
profile.scope: The fictional case contains the company’s pilot description and the inspector’s acceptance record.

documents.name: Cedar pilot status and scope
documents.limitations: Fictional captured evidence used only to exercise the offline assessment.

documents.name: Cedar pilot inspection and acceptance
documents.limitations: Fictional captured evidence used only to exercise the offline assessment.

evidence.title: Cedar pilot status and scope
evidence.extract: The company records a supervised one-shift manufacturing pilot without documented sales or committed funding.

evidence.title: Cedar pilot inspection and acceptance
evidence.extract: The inspector confirmed prototype acceptance under the one-shift trial criteria. There is insufficient evidence on sustained line throughput or manufacturing cost.

thesis.management: The supervised pilot can transition to larger lots.
thesis.independent: The independent inspection confirms prototype acceptance in one shift. The larger-lot claim remains untested.
falsifiers: An amended inspection or failed retest under the same conditions would change the acceptance finding. Multi-shift logs would allow a separate conclusion about scale.

safeguards.rationale: The scope of this fixture is defined by the supplied packet.

factors.question: Which legal entity owns the product, contracts and securities?
factors.finding: The pilot brief names Cedar. It does not identify the asset owner or securities issuer.
factors.impact: Ownership of the proposed financing vehicle is unconfirmed.
factors.next_test: Match the registered entity to the share register and equipment titles.

factors.question: Who has demonstrated demand or willingness to pay for the current offer?
factors.finding: Neither record shows a customer order or payment.
factors.impact: Prototype acceptance has not established a paying buyer.
factors.next_test: Obtain a purchase order and evidence of the customer’s payment terms.

factors.question: What did Cedar deliver during the supervised shift?
factors.finding: The inspector accepted the prototype produced during the supervised shift.
factors.impact: Cedar demonstrated delivery under those trial conditions. Output on an ordinary shift is unknown.
factors.next_test: Repeat the run at normal staffing and record good units and rejects.

factors.question: Who controls delivery and decisions, and what track record is evidenced?
factors.finding: The trial names no manager accountable for running a multi-shift line.
factors.impact: Responsibility for staffing and commissioning an expansion is unverified.
factors.next_test: Identify the operations lead and verify experience commissioning a comparable line.

factors.question: Which alternatives compete for the same buyer and budget?
factors.finding: No competing supplier quote or buyer specification accompanies the inspection.
factors.impact: An attainable price and buyer preference remain unknown.
factors.next_test: Compare supplier quotes against the same lot, specification and delivery date.

factors.question: What drives recognised revenue and contribution at the current stage?
factors.finding: The company provided no pilot invoice or collection record.
factors.impact: The trial cannot be counted as revenue or used to infer gross margin.
factors.next_test: Match a signed purchase order to acceptance, billing and receipt.

factors.question: Which dated cash and funding constraints affect the next decision?
factors.finding: The records contain no opening bank balance or committed funding.
factors.impact: Cash available for placing equipment orders is unknown.
factors.next_test: Reconcile bank balances, restrictions and supplier deposit dates.

factors.question: What evidence suggests an advantage can survive replication or switching?
factors.finding: The inspection reports acceptance but gives no comparison of competing processes or ownership of the design.
factors.impact: A buyer’s switching cost and Cedar’s ability to defend its design are unknown.
factors.next_test: Review design ownership and compare a rival’s ability to meet the same specification.

factors.question: Which operational, regulatory or other dependencies could prevent delivery?
factors.finding: The trial records omit supplier commitments, production permits and warranty obligations.
factors.impact: A dependency could delay the first commercial lot.
factors.next_test: Check lead times, capacity commitments and obligations attached to the first order.

factors.question: What observable change would invalidate the independent case or valuation basis?
factors.finding: There is no multi-shift cost record or evidence of an agreed sale price.
factors.impact: A valuation based on scaled output cannot yet use a defensible unit margin.
factors.next_test: Compare cost per saleable unit at production scale with a dated buyer quote.

factors.question: What effective capacity and first-pass yield are demonstrated?
factors.finding: One supervised shift met the acceptance criteria. The inspector gives no sustained throughput or cost.
factors.impact: Monthly saleable output cannot be extrapolated from this run.
factors.next_test: Compare good units, rework, scrap and downtime across representative shifts.

factors.question: How much capital and working capital are needed at the planned scale?
factors.finding: No equipment quote, supplier credit terms or inventory cycle was provided.
factors.impact: The expansion cash requirement and deposit dates are unknown.
factors.next_test: Obtain itemised equipment quotes, supplier milestones and the intended inventory cycle.

factors.question: Which trials or validations establish production readiness?
factors.finding: The inspector confirmed prototype acceptance at trial settings. Sustained production has not been demonstrated.
factors.impact: The trial establishes a technical milestone. It does not establish a production commitment.
factors.next_test: Repeat the acceptance test across larger lots at planned staffing and line speed.

factors.question: Which evidence, use of funds and milestones are needed for fundraising readiness?
factors.finding: Cedar has a prototype milestone but no funded commissioning schedule.
factors.impact: The timing and size of the raise depend on equipment deposits, working capital and delivery lead times.
factors.next_test: Build a dated uses-of-funds schedule and stress supplier delays.

factors.question: What did the pilot actually prove and what would convert it to commercial use?
factors.finding: The prototype met the one-shift test. There is no contract converting acceptance into a commercial order.
factors.impact: The next milestone is an accepted paid lot under repeatable conditions.
factors.next_test: Confirm the buyer’s acceptance and payment terms and test a representative lot.

research.reason: One document gives the declared identity. The register is still required.
Cedar’s brief and the inspector describe the same one-shift acceptance. Neither record covers later shifts.
Available review covers one shift. More interpretation of this trial cannot establish representative yield.
Equipment quotations and a staged funding model were outside the supplied packet.
Independent buying alternatives require external search beyond this packet.
Confirm who owns the manufacturing entity before attributing management or supplier commitments.
Trial records do not resolve durable differentiation.

challenges.finding: Initial wording could imply operating capacity beyond pilot scale.
challenges.correction: Rechecked inspection scope and classified commercial maturity as pilot.

challenges.finding: Opening cash and equipment commitments prevent linked scenarios.
challenges.correction: Withhold forecast and reconcile cash and capital commitments when supplied.

gaps.item: Cash, equipment quotations and funding milestones
gaps.period: At 27 November 2026 and each proposed equipment payment date
gaps.why: Current resources and supplier financing capacity are unknown.
gaps.conclusion: How much cash Cedar needs before equipment can be commissioned and when a round must close.
gaps.action: Stress the forecast with equipment lead times and test downside cash requirements.

gaps.item: Repeat multi-shift production and reject logs
gaps.period: Representative shifts and lots at the intended staffing and line speed
gaps.why: The one-shift trial does not establish sustainable throughput or yield.
gaps.conclusion: How many saleable units Cedar can promise per month and whether the line is ready for larger orders.
gaps.action: Compare good units, downtime and rework under representative production conditions.

gaps.item: Invoices, paid status and collections from the pilot
gaps.period: From the pilot order through acceptance, invoicing and collection
gaps.why: There is no reconciliation between trial work and recognised commercial activity.
gaps.conclusion: Whether the trial generated revenue or secured a paid commercial order.
gaps.action: Verify acceptance obligations, billing dates and actual collection.

gaps.item: Dated legal entity registration and issued securities
gaps.why: The company brief gives the name but ownership and issued shares are unconfirmed.
gaps.conclusion: Which entity can issue shares and who would be diluted by the round.
gaps.action: Reconcile company registry, securities register and proposed issuer.

decision.conclusion: The inspector accepted the prototype during one supervised shift (E2). Obtain repeat production logs, equipment quotations and opening cash before sizing the expansion round.
decision.limitations: The two fictional records cover one supervised shift. Web research and outreach were unavailable.
strengths: The independent inspection corroborates acceptance under the stated trial conditions.
risks: A successful prototype run gives no saleable units per month, unit cost or committed sales.

scenarios.rationale: No opening cash schedule or equipment commitments.

cap_table.rationale: No verified security register or financing terms.

research_plan.objective_rationale: Assess the evidence and capital milestones needed before a financing process.
research_plan.stage_rationale: An independent inspector accepted one supervised shift. No repeat orders or paid output were documented.
research_plan.limitations: Only frozen synthetic packet records were reviewed. Web research and outreach were unavailable.

questions.question: Which legal entity owns the product, contracts and securities?
questions.evidence_required: Dated registration, ownership and entity perimeter matched to the assessed business.
questions.counter_test: Check similarly named entities, former names and mismatch between invoices, product and fundraising entity.
questions.decision_use: Establish the entity, ownership, and transaction eligibility.

questions.question: Did the inspected prototype meet the one-shift trial criteria?
questions.evidence_required: The dated trial description and the inspector’s acceptance under the same operating conditions.
questions.counter_test: Check whether the inspection covered a single shift, rework or any subsequent production lots.
questions.decision_use: Determine whether prototype acceptance can count as a completed fundraising milestone.

questions.question: What effective capacity and first-pass yield are demonstrated?
questions.evidence_required: Production and quality records at specified shifts, product mix and utilisation.
questions.counter_test: Compare rated capacity with downtime, scrap, rework and changeovers.
questions.decision_use: Test deliverable volume and direct cost assumptions.

questions.question: Which dated cash and funding constraints affect the next decision?
questions.evidence_required: Unrestricted cash, commitments, cash movement and timing or a precise request for the missing records.
questions.counter_test: Test restricted cash, delayed collections and conditional finance against the same timeline.
questions.decision_use: Determine funding needs, liquidity exposure and timing.

questions.question: What drives recognised revenue and contribution at the current stage?
questions.evidence_required: Revenue mechanism and reconciled operating inputs where available, with actual, contracted and projected amounts identified.
questions.counter_test: Look for refundable deposits, free pilots, bookings and pass-through amounts presented as earned revenue.
questions.decision_use: Set revenue quality and defensible unit-economics assumptions.

questions.question: Who has demonstrated demand or willingness to pay for the current offer?
questions.evidence_required: Segment-specific demand evidence that distinguishes interest, use, purchase and repeat use.
questions.counter_test: Find inactive users, rejected offers, unpaid pilots and alternatives purchasers already use.
questions.decision_use: Test demand and reachable customer segments.

questions.question: Who controls delivery and decisions, and what track record is evidenced?
questions.evidence_required: Named responsibilities, relevant execution history and decision rights.
questions.counter_test: Check contradictory biographies, conflicts and departures that change who can deliver.
questions.decision_use: Assess execution, governance and key-person dependencies.

questions.question: What evidence suggests an advantage can survive replication or switching?
questions.evidence_required: Customer behaviour, protected rights or operational economics that can be traced to the advantage.
questions.counter_test: Identify reproducible features, weak IP coverage, multi-homing and low switching costs.
questions.decision_use: Test durability and the persistence of value drivers.
